Every day, thousands of local homeowners search online for electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, and roofers. The question is: are they finding your business or your competitors?

Digital advertising has transformed how contractors attract new customers. Unlike traditional marketing methods like yard signs or newspaper ads, online advertising puts your business directly in front of high-intent customers actively searching for your services. The contractors who master these platforms consistently fill their schedules with profitable jobs.

But with so many advertising options available, choosing the right platform can feel overwhelming. Should you invest in Google Ads? Try Facebook advertising? What about those Local Service Ads you keep hearing about?

This guide breaks down the best digital advertising platforms for contractors, explaining how each works, what results you can expect, and how to allocate your marketing budget for maximum return on investment.

## **Why Digital Advertising Matters for Contractors**

The contractor industry has shifted dramatically toward digital-first customer acquisition. According to [Google’s consumer insights](https://www.thinkwithgoogle.com/consumer-insights/consumer-trends/), 97% of consumers search online for local businesses, and 78% of local mobile searches result in an offline purchase within 24 hours.

![](https://contractormarketingpros.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/users-search.webp?wsr)

For contractors, this means your next customer is likely searching for services right now. Digital advertising allows you to:

*   **Target high-intent customers** actively searching for your specific services
*   **Control your geographic reach** to focus on profitable service areas
*   **Track every lead** from first click to booked job
*   **Scale your marketing** based on capacity and seasonality
*   **Outperform competitors** who rely solely on word-of-mouth

The contractors generating consistent leads understand that [paid advertising services](https://contractormarketingpros.net/services/paid-ads/) deliver predictable, measurable results that other marketing methods simply cannot match.

## **Google Ads: The Foundation of Contractor Advertising**

Google Ads remains the most powerful digital advertising platform for contractors because it captures customers at the moment of intent. When someone searches “emergency plumber near me” or “AC repair today,” they need your services immediately.

### **Search Ads**

Search ads appear at the top of Google results when users type specific keywords. For contractors, this means showing up first when homeowners need:

*   Emergency repairs (water leaks, electrical issues, HVAC failures)
*   Scheduled services (installations, replacements, inspections)
*   Seasonal maintenance (furnace tune-ups, AC check-ups)

**Best practices for contractor search ads:**

*   Focus on service-specific keywords rather than broad terms
*   Include your service area in ad copy
*   Use call extensions for immediate phone leads
*   Create separate campaigns for emergency versus scheduled services
*   Set appropriate bid adjustments for mobile devices

In our reading, most construction "bid" searches come from contractors looking for work, not owners looking for a builder.

results.title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns
results.markdown:
Title: About Quality Score for Search campaigns

URL Source: https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118

Markdown Content:
Quality Score is a diagnostic tool meant to give you a sense of how well your [ad quality](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/156066) compares to other advertisers.

This score is measured on a scale from 1-10 and available at the keyword level. A higher Quality Score means that your ad and landing page are more relevant and useful to someone searching for your keyword, compared to other advertisers.

You can use the Quality Score diagnostic tool to identify where it might be beneficial to improve your ads, landing pages, or keyword selection.

**On this page**

*   [Calculate Quality Score](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118#calculate_score)
*   [Check Quality Score](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118#check_qs)

**Good to know about Quality Score**

*   Quality Score is not a key performance indicator and should not be optimized or aggregated with the rest of your data.
*   Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction. It’s a diagnostic tool to identify how ads that show for certain keywords affect the user experience.

* * *

## [](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118)How it’s calculated

Quality Score is calculated based on the combined performance of 3 components:

*   **Expected clickthrough rate (CTR)**: The likelihood that your ad will be clicked when shown.
*   **Ad relevance**: How closely your ad matches the intent behind a user's search.
*   **Landing page experience**: How relevant and useful your landing page is to people who click your ad.

Each component is evaluated with a status of “Above average,” “Average,” or “Below average.” This evaluation is based on a comparison with other advertisers whose ads showed for the exact same search over the last 90 days.

A broad match keyword may have a Quality Score even though it has no impressions as long as there is a corresponding exact match keyword with impressions in the last 90 days. If there are impressions for searches that exactly match a broad match keyword through an exact match keyword in the same ad group, this will report the same Quality Score for both of the keywords.

If one of these components has a status of “Average” or “Below average”, this may indicate an opportunity to make improvements. Learn more about [5 ways to use Quality Score to improve your performance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167130).

### Keep in mind

*   Quality Score is based on **historical impressions for exact searches**of your keyword, therefore changing keyword match types will not impact Quality Score.
*   If you notice a “—” in the Quality Score column, it means there aren't enough searches that exactly match your keywords to determine a keyword’s Quality Score. To help gather traffic data and resolve this status: 
    *   **Use Keyword Planner to discover higher-volume keywords:** Identify relevant search terms with sufficient search volume.
    *   **Broaden match types:** While match types don't change how your Quality Score is calculated, broadening them helps your keyword participate in more auctions, increasing the chances of gathering enough exact-match search data to generate a score.

*   There are factors related to your ad quality that might not be captured by Quality Score. These factors include, but are not limited to: 
    *   Devices used in search
    *   Location of user
    *   Time of day
    *   Assets

*   Information obtained from any of Google's various [crawlers](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/crawling/overview-google-crawlers)may be used to assess ad quality, which can be reflected through Quality Score.

* * *

## [](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167118)How to check your Quality Score

1.   Go to [**Keywords**](https://ads.google.com/aw/keywords) within the **Campaigns** menu ![Image 1: Campaigns Icon](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/PYU3UjHzepAdY-dWS9ObIzq9WgLGS0SZeJS1hQ0Be3fxCIUQZaWCrR4HoYqriXSEbQ=w40).
2.   In the upper right corner of the table, select the columns icon ![Image 2: A picture of the Google Ads columns icon](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/poJPSxxmyG5nyGxTbdiUmvgDuTZF5IHNddHCp2_gGuax6_nG4coJefjn7KKwJfWu4c8=w50) .
3.   Under “Modify columns for keywords”, select the drop-down arrow beside “All columns” and open the Quality score section.
4.   To add the current Quality Score and its component statuses as new columns in the keyword reporting table, select any of the following: 
    *   Quality Score
    *   Landing Page Exp.
    *   Exp. CTR
    *   Ad Relevance

5.   To view past Quality Score stats for the reporting period you’re looking at, choose any of the following metrics. To add past Quality Score data and its component statuses as new columns in the keyword reporting table, select the following: 
    *   Quality Score (hist.)
    *   Landing Page Exper. (hist.)
    *   Ad Relevance (hist.)
    *   Exp. CTR. (hist.) You can view the change in daily scores by segmenting your table by day. 

6.   Select **Apply**.

* * *

### Related links

*   [5 ways to use Quality Score to improve your performance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6167130)
*   [About ad quality](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/156066)
